newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DELIGHTED WENGER PRAISES ARSENAL'S FIGHTING SPIRIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DELIGHTED WENGER PRAISES ARSENAL'S FIGHTING SPIRIT.

text.p: Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger praised his team's fighting spirit after they defied the odds to beat Newcastle 2-1 and replace Kevin Keegan's side at the top of the English premier league on Saturday.
The London side were reduced to 10 men for the second successive match after skipper Tony Adams was sent off for grappling with his England team mate Alan Shearer midway through the first half.

Wenger replaced forward John Hartson with defender Andy Linighan to fill the defensive hole left by Adams's departure and Arsenal survived an almost constant bombardment from the league leaders to escape with three points after Ian Wright grabbed what proved to be the winner after an hour.

For a while in the closing stages Arsenal had only nine men on the field after Lee Dixon, who put them ahead with an 11th minute header, was stretchered off. He returned to the fray for the last few minutes.

Shearer, who had scored in every home league match he has played for Newcastle since his world record 15.0 million pounds ($25 million) transfer from Blackburn in the summer, maintained that record with Newcastle's equaliser after 21 minutes.

The odds were certainly tipped Newcastle's way after Adams dismissal but, despite attacking almost non-stop for the rest of the match, they could not break down Arsenal again, and Wright, playing alone up front, scored with Arsenal's only real break of the second half.

Although he was lucky that he was able to control a mishit Paul Merson shot that ran into his path, he took his 19th goal of the season with style, firing a left-footed low cross-shot wide of goalkeeper Pavel Srnicek.

"I am never surprised when Ian scores -- and neither is anyone else in England," said Wenger, "but it was a collective team effort and we played with a great fighting spirit. I have to congratulate my players. We did not panic at the back."
Arsenal's title odds were cut from 6-1 to 4-1 following the win but the title race is still wide open, with any one of seven teams in with a chance.
One of those must be fourth-placed Wimbledon. They stretched their unbeaten run to 17 matches with a 1-0 win over bottom-placed Nottingham Forest who have now gone 14 league matches without a win.
Robbie Earle's 37th minute goal gave Wimbledon their win and put them on 28 points -- the same as third-placed Liverpool who play at Tottenham on Monday.

Champions Manchester United warmed up for their Champions' League clash with Rapid Vienna on Wednesday with a 3-1 win over Leicester who had beaten a weakened United side 2-0 in the League Cup on Wednesday.

A full-strength United took 75 minutes to break down Leicester's resilience, Nicky Butt scoring. Norwegian Ole Solskjaer and Butt added two more in the last five minutes, Nicky Lennon netting a last-minute consolation for Leicester.
The shock result of the day was at Goodison where Sunderland, without a goal in six away league matches, won 3-1 at Everton who had not lost for eight games.
Sunderland manager Peter Reid saw his side go ahead against the team he used to play for through Craig Russell after 54 minutes.

Second-half substitute Duncan Ferguson headed an equaliser after 64 minutes but two late goals from 18-year-old Michael Bridges gave Sunderland their win. Graham Stuart also missed a penalty for Everton just after the interval.

Blackburn's recent revival continued with a 2-1 win over Southampton who had Dutchman Ulrich Van Gobbel sent off after 81 minutes. Six minutes later Chris Sutton scored Blackburn's winner which lifted them to 18th -- their highest position since August 26. Coventry, who lost 2-1 at Derby, slipped to 19th -- just one place and one point better than Forest.
